about.title: About me
about.lead: I’m Eli, an early-career cybersecurity candidate from Northern Israel. I’m building toward a Blue Team role, starting from hands-on support work.
about.story1: My first technical role was Tier 1 support at Cellcom. Every call was a small investigation: check connectivity, rule out DNS, look at the Wi-Fi and the home equipment, then fix it or escalate it with clear notes. Handling a steady volume of these taught me to stay calm under time pressure and to document properly.
about.story2: Those habits are exactly what a SOC runs on, so I went deeper. I completed a Blue Team course on the SOC track at Cyber Gain Center, where I investigated security events in Splunk and QRadar, analysed traffic in Wireshark, worked with FortiGate, and practised Active Directory administration in Windows and Linux labs. I also earned the EC-Council Certified SOC Analyst (C|SA) credential.
about.story3: I’m now looking for an entry-level role in a SOC, help desk, desktop support or NOC team, where I can keep learning on real systems. Alongside security, I build websites using AI-assisted development tools.

troubleshoot.title: Methodical troubleshooting
troubleshoot.body: Start from the symptom, test one layer at a time, and confirm the fix before closing.

document.title: Clear documentation and escalation
document.body: Write tickets the next person can act on, and escalate with the evidence already attached.

learn.title: Learning in labs
learn.body: Practise detection and investigation hands-on, and build on what each lab teaches.

cellcom.p1: Supported customers with internet, communications and TV services: connectivity checks, TCP/IP and DNS troubleshooting, Wi-Fi and home network equipment.
cellcom.p2: Documented service calls, followed them through to resolution and escalated complex faults to technical teams in a structured way.
cellcom.p3: Worked in a fast multitasking environment under time pressure while keeping service quality high.
cellcom.metrics: Handled about 50 cases per day with a 95% first-contact resolution rate (self-reported).

cyberGain.p1: Monitored and investigated security events in SIEM platforms (Splunk, QRadar).
cyberGain.p2: Network security with FortiGate and traffic analysis with Wireshark.
cyberGain.p3: IT and help desk labs: Active Directory, Windows and Linux, remote support and user management.
cyberGain.p4: Python and PowerShell scripts to automate administrative tasks in Windows and Active Directory.
